body.content: Distinguishing independent vs. pseudo-uncorrelated failures: Independent failures show a Poisson distribution over time. Pseudo-uncorrelated failures (hidden shared cause) exhibit 'burstiness' or 'clustering' when triggered by an external event (e.g., a leap second, a specific API update), even if the services appear unrelated.
body.why_keep_this: Addresses the second part of the problem regarding evidence for distinguishing failure modes.

body.content: Exploring the 'Economic Homogeneity' hypothesis: Do market pressures force small, independent operators to adopt the same 'best-of-breed' tools, thereby creating an accidental monolith at the infrastructure layer? If so, 'independence' is an organizational illusion that doesn't translate to technical resilience.
body.why_keep_this: Connects the economic reality of service operation to the technical failure modes.

body.content: Hypothesizing a 'Correlation Horizon': the point where adding more redundancy to a single service actually increases the risk of a correlated crash due to the complexity of the coordination logic (e.g., consensus algorithms like Paxos/Raft failing under specific network partitions).
body.why_keep_this: Provides a counter-intuitive mechanism for why 'more redundancy' might be worse.
